**Goal.** Add a spatial field on top of the stage-3 truth, then account for it with Hefley-style basis functions. Ramp the field from weak to strongly spatial (including a gradient aligned with DistReef), and show which estimates survive, which don't, and whether the authors' diagnostics would notice.

## Checklist

- [ ] Reading: Hefley, Model Specifications + Equivalent Specifications (Eqs. 4–13)
- [ ] The Q2 location intercept as a basis model (ZZ′)
- [ ] Collinearity: location-level covariates vs space
- [ ] Write `sim_spatial()` in `sim/sim_spatial.R`
- [ ] Fit the stage-3 GAM (no space), then add a spatial basis
- [ ] Ramp: spatial variance and range; DistReef-aligned scenario
- [ ] Diagnostics: Moran's I and bubble-plot detection rate

```{r}
#| label: setup
source("../sim/_load.R")
library(glmmTMB)
library(mgcv)
HTrees2 <- read.table(file.path(data_dir, "abundance.only.natural.trees.txt"),
                      header = TRUE, dec = ".")
```

## 1. Reading: Hefley's specifications

Read Model Specifications and Equivalent Specifications (Eqs. 4–13). Write out the Q2 indicator Z (48 × 24) in words, and multiply out ZZ′ for a small piece of it in `notes/derivations.qmd`.

**Done when:** you can say which of Eqs. 4–13 *is* `mod2`'s random intercept, and what changes when Var(α) stops being σ²I.
